name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Auto-apply trivial style/doc fixes (trailing whitespace, basic formatting) directly to the repo. This keeps the codebase clean without human review overhead, freeing the team to focus on meaningful work. The trade-off is accepting a small risk of unintended changes—mitigated by limiting scope to non-logic edits.

name: Gauge
text: Auto-applying *any* trivial fix normalizes sloppy reviews—PR-Agent’s 90% threshold proves it. Better: auto-apply *only* non-controversial, zero-risk changes (e.g., license headers) and require human review for style/doc tweaks. Settle it with a test: run the auto-fix on a stale branch and measure unintended diffs—if >0.1% of lines change, reject the idea.

name: Gauge
text: Auto-applying *any* style/doc tweaks via PR-Agent still risks normalizing sloppy reviews—its 90% threshold means 1 in 10 changes could introduce noise, and humans will stop questioning trivial PRs. Better: auto-apply *only* license headers or copyright updates (zero-risk) and require human review for all style/doc changes; settle it by running a 30-day trial on a stale branch and measuring unintended merge conflicts or review fatigue.
